changes.reason: Only hintCore changed. New hint sends the child to the offer that spans l.14-15 and to the clause just before it (l.14, 'nothing on her wall but a calendar'): it points to the evidence without stating the key's content, which is what the hold asked for.

Only the held distractor changed. 'He told Nan he was going to Ryan's' is false: l.17 has him tell Mum, and nothing gives Nan the Ryan's story (l.14-15 has him tell Nan only that he would get a picture). Tag en-attribute-transfer fits (Mum's detail moved onto Nan); execution true (Nan fills l.15-16).
Only hintCore changed. New hint points to l.29 and asks what the elder is doing (growing out of the wall) without naming it a plant, so it no longer selects the key by category.
Only hintCore changed. Substitution move ('try each answer in place of the effect on line 32') rules nothing out by name; the dominant-sense distractor is no longer coached away.

Rebuild was needed: the old key ('the water he watches is the slow one') was not supported, and the stem's 'settle' asserted a conclusion. New stem and key are true of l.33-35 ('I understood it was not going to stop doing that for me'); lineRefs narrowed to 33-35 to match the stem. Every new execution checked: Nan's one-night telling is at l.10-11 (outside the window); 'a minute later it came further up' is l.34, so the water is coming in; 'not going to stop' is at l.34-35 and the option states the affirmative. Same type and tier kept, though the inference is short (the stem echoes 'I understood').
Only hintCore changed. New hint sends the child to l.40-41 for what made the picture hard to take, without saying how many causes there are, so it no longer names a property only the key has.

The hold named only the missing referent for 'them' in distractor 2. The proposal changes that option from 'He tells the whole of it the way his Nan has always told it to them.' to 'He tells all of it the way Nan has always told it to him.' It also rewords 'the whole of it' to 'all of it' and drops 'his' from 'his Nan'. Neither change bears on the fault, and the why does not disclose them: it claims the change is 'now told it to him' (value only). This is needless restyling of correct wording. Re-propose with only them->him changed. The hintCore change is sound.

The defensible fear distractor is replaced by 'The barrel shook as the man leaned on it'. That is true at l.9-10 and gives no reason for staying hidden, and en-inference-literal-lookalike fits. The hint no longer coaches away fear: it points to 'for' on l.13 ('curiosity, for from these dozen words'), which introduces the reason. The last sentence of the walkScript asserted that fear was not the reason, which is the doubtful claim the hold names, so replacing it was needed. The new sentence is true.

Execution only. The false boilerplate sentence and the truncated quotation are removed. What remains is true: Dick square is at l.37 and the keg is at l.56, both outside 18-26 and 43-49. The added clause 'so neither half compares the two speeches' is true and completes the explanation.

The defensible praise distractor is replaced by 'It has put him off the job'. That is false: l.27-28 'didn't half a quarter like the job till I had this talk... but there's my hand on it now'. en-relation-word-flipped fits, because reading 'till' as 'because' keeps the facts and reverses how they relate. The execution is true.
Only hintCore changed. The hint now gives the line a referent by what Hands says there ('had enough of the captain', l.41) and keeps the same move. It does not paraphrase the key.

The partly supported doubt distractor and its untrue execution are replaced. 'They were strong enough to carry him out' is contradicted by l.52-53 ('if I had found the strength'), and the execution is true. The new hintCore ('Read line 52 first. Ask what kept him from leaping out.') sends the child to the context without eliminating options by category or ignoring the heart.

Both faults the hold names are fixed. The hint is now a sampling move that names neither half of the key. In the walkScript, 'he cannot move' at l.32-33 becomes 'still in the barrel', which is true. Nothing else in the walkScript changed.

Only hintCore changed. The false claim that two options are true is gone. The new hint sends the child to the decision at l.4 and on to the end of that sentence at l.6 ('so as to give her a decent appearance when Herr Sesemann returned'). That points to evidence without stating the key.

The walkScript now cites the right lines and quotes exactly. 'what do I see at the bottom but a heap of rolls' runs over l.11-12, and 'a whole pile of bread' is verbatim at l.13. The new quotation is declared, which is needed because the walkScript quotes it. The truncated fragment is gone from the hat-option execution, and the added locator ('where Tinette is told to take it away', l.13-15) is true.

Most of the change is sound and needed. 'Nobody touched it, and it stayed where it was' is contradicted by the table at l.15 and the counterpane at l.42-43. 'these lines never say who' is true of l.13-15 and 42-43, and l.39-41 imply Sebastian. The hint and walkScript had to change because they referred to the removed distractor and the over-strong 'nothing between them says who'. But the key also changes from 'Somebody has put it back' to 'Somebody has given it back to her'. The hold did not name that verb, it was not wrong, and the why does not disclose the change: it presents the key edit as only 'these lines never say who' in place of 'the passage'. Needless restyling of correct key wording. Re-propose keeping 'Somebody has put it back'.
Only hintCore changed. The hint is now two grammatical sentences. 'depend upon it' is on l.33 and 'Clara's promise' on l.32 is what 'it' refers to. It does not define the word.

The window is fixed. The reason ('to make sure that she could depend upon it') is at l.33, and the stem, lineRefs and orderAnchor now cover l.33-36. The walkScript no longer calls l.35 a repeated question: it cites l.33 for the reason and l.34 for the question, and both are true.

Only hintCore changed. The substitution move no longer eliminates the dominant-sense distractor by name. I checked the drafter's claim against the packet: the stored 'press down hard' option already carries en-vocab-built-from-parts, and its execution describes building a meaning from 'press', so the tag mismatch in the hold is already resolved and options correctly stay unchanged.
Execution only. The false sentence placing the message at l.40 is removed. What remains ('True at line 37, before this window, and it is not what he points at') is true.

The second correct answer ('made it more out of shape still in her joy', running onto l.44) is replaced by 'She finds it lying under the counterpane'. That is true only at l.42-43, before the window, and it is how she comes on the hat, not what she does with it. en-wrong-scope-retrieval fits, and the execution is true.

The true distractor (bread taken, hat returns) is replaced by 'taken gently... sharp words'. That is false: Rottenmeier speaks 'in a determined tone' (l.19), and Sebastian's signs mean 'Don't you be unhappy!' (l.40-41). en-attribute-transfer fits, because the two manners are swapped between the two people. The hint no longer sends the child to a verdict line that does not exist. The walkScript's line-41 claim was untrue, since the hat is back at l.42, and correcting it was needed for the row to be accurate.
Only hintCore changed. The substitution move ('try each answer in place of wont on line 11') no longer rules out the won't-lookalike the item tests, and it names no option.

The reframe was needed. Under 'Why is the narrator glad', being spared the sight is the stated reason (l.19-20). The portrait option was a second answer and the irony option nearly one, so replacing one distractor would not have closed the fault. The new stem is answered by l.20-21 ('a man of quick temper, and perhaps he would not have taken it so placidly as I did'). The key's 'might' keeps the text's 'perhaps', which the old 'would not have borne' dropped. Both new distractors are false. 'as calmly as the narrator did' drops the 'not' of l.21. 'glad to see his brother so loved' is contradicted by 'unpleasant sight' (l.20) and 'ironical sort of greeting' (l.19). The irony execution is realigned and true at l.19. The hint referred to options that are gone. The walkScript no longer says 'hot temper', and 'easily angered' is a true paraphrase of 'quick temper'. The why discloses all of this.

Execution only. The false boilerplate sentence and its fragment are removed. What remains is true: the kneeling is at l.37, after the walk up the nave at l.26-27. The added 'well past this window' is true.

Both faults the hold names are fixed. The execution's false sentence quoting the organ is removed, and what remains is true: the oath is at l.39, before the heralds at l.41. The hintCore no longer states the key's content. It now points to the heralds on l.41 and on to l.42.

The stem is fixed. It now asks what the lines show about what the Duke feels and thinks, which takes in 'looked to the right and to the left, as a man looks who thinks on flight' (l.53-54), the source of the key's second half. The face-option execution had to change because it answered the old stem. Its new line range (l.54-55, 'face was patched / with red and white') is correct. The false hint ('Two of these describe him without saying why') is replaced by a move.

The hold's hint fault is fixed, but the unchanged walkScript misreads 'even then'. It says the light (l.40) and his hands (l.41) are 'two things going against him', then 'The words even then join them. They mean the second happened despite the first.' In l.41-42, 'even then' joins holding the phone in both hands to the picture still coming out shaken. It does not join the light and the hands, and nothing in l.40-42 says the hands happened despite the light. Key and distractors check against l.40-42.

Row as proposed reads correctly: present-tense sentences (l.1, 6-9, 13, 16, 18, 28-29, 36-37, 42-43) are all still true and the walk is past, so the key holds; summary, Nan's-way (story changes at l.10, reread at l.38) and Nan-present/his-past (l.9 and l.18 are his, in the present) all wrong; hint is a move. Does not land while the change is REFUSED.

Key matches l.13-14 'the lives of all the honest men aboard depended upon me alone'; about-to-jump-up (l.10, what he nearly did), treasure (not given) and barrel-shook (l.9-10, no reason) are not reasons; no remaining option is a defensible feeling-as-reason; hint points to the connective, not the content.

Key checks against l.21-22 (puts it all away) and l.44-47 (Smollett sails, squire and doctor find the stuff); rough/pay both from first speech (l.18-20); Dick/keg outside windows (l.37, 56); spends-all contradicted by l.20-22; hint and walkScript accurate.
